chapter: Bird, Coltrane and Dinah Washington recollections
title: Jimmy Heath and Lexington
summary: Cobb discusses Jimmy Heath, who went to Lexington, and praises his autobiography.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, Jimmy Heath was – Jimmy Heath went to the – at one time they was calling Jimmy Heath “Little Bird.” I guess Jimmy just got to tenor. He was playing tenor. He was – Jimmy was a bandleader way back there. Before Percy started to play the bass, Jimmy was a bandleader. Percy used to carry his horn around. That’s how long ago he’s been out there doing it. Then he went to college for that long time, and he came back out.
You mean the university? That special university?
Yeah, he went to the university.
That’s right. That’s what he calls it. He says, “I went to college.” Saved his life.
That’s right. Saved his life. It’s a good thing, too, because he could have really been gone for 40 years by now. It really did him good. He talks about it too. He’s not ashamed about nothing.
I was in the – I just finished his book, and I was – I didn’t really know the extent of, in going back, the kind of things – he doesn’t hide anything about . . .
No, he’s just right on it. Tells it like it is, like it was. I love James.
